rows.reconciliation: page 38, the row `Totals`: levy_percent 100.0 vs printed 100.0 ; tax_levy 29,956,477.18 vs printed 28,054,406.88 ; valuation 1,742,668,758.0 vs printed 1,548,256,450.0
rows.proof: `Town of Lunenburg - Board of Assessors / Fiscal 2021 Assessments and Revenues by Major Class`, PDF page 38 of the FY2021 annual town report (printed folio 37). Four property classes and a Totals line, read off the rendered page. LEVY PERCENT CLOSES EXACTLY: 91.0772 + 4.3140 + 1.4121 + 3.1967 = 100.0000 against the printed `100%`. THE OTHER TWO COLUMNS DO NOT, AND THE DOCUMENT IS WHAT DOES NOT ADD UP. The four valuations come to 1,742,668,758.00 against a printed Totals of 1,548,256,450, and the four levies to 29,956,477.18 against a printed 28,054,406.88. The reading is not in doubt: each class's own valuation x 17.19 / 1000 is its own printed levy to the cent, and each class's share of 29,956,477.18 is its own printed Levy Percent to four decimals -- so the four rows are consistent with each other and with the rate, and only the Totals line is not. WHAT THE DATA SHOWS, and nothing further: the two printed Totals figures, 1,548,256,450 and 28,054,406.88, are to the cent the Totals the FY2020 report prints, where they foot FY2020's own four classes exactly (1,404,806,468 + 73,878,632 + 25,130,800 + 44,440,550) at FY2020's rate of 18.12. WHAT IT DOES NOT SHOW: why. Nothing here establishes whether the line was carried over, recomputed, or means something else. AND A THIRD FIGURE IS IN PLAY: the prose above the table says `The tax rate went from $18.12 to $17.74 for FY 2021`, where the table prints 17.19 in every row.

rows.proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG / TRUST AND OPEB FUNDS / FISCAL YEAR 2021 SUMMARY, Page 1 of 2`, PDF page 40 of the FY2021 annual town report (printed folio 39). The page prints three groups -- CEMETERY FUNDS (3), CONSERVATION FUNDS (5) and LIBRARY FUNDS (14) -- each with its own SUBTOTALS line, so each group is read as its own group and footed to the subtotal the page prints for it. Page 2 of 2 is PDF page 41 and is proved separately by `stabilization-balances`. READ, NOT RECOGNISED: pdfplumber returns 0 words on this page. TEN COLUMNS, NAMED FROM THE PRINTED HEADER AND NOT INFERRED (rule 13b.4), left to right: BEGINNING MARKET VALUE, BEGINNING PRINCIPAL, BEGINNING EARNINGS, NET EARNINGS, TRANSFERS OF PRINCIPAL, TRANSFERS OF EARNINGS, ENDING CASH VALUE, CHANGE IN UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS, UNREALIZED GAIN/LOSS, ENDING MARKET VALUE. Every one is headed `FY 2021`. FOUR ASSERTIONS, ALL TO THE CENT AND WITH NO TOLERANCE BEYOND A HALF-CENT: the three identities every row states about itself (declared below as `row_identity`), and each of the ten columns added down against the group's printed SUBTOTALS. Across the whole page that is 96 independent assertions -- 22 funds x 3 row identities, plus 10 columns x 3 group subtotals -- and all 96 close exactly. The third identity is the one that matters most, because it ties the two ends of a row together through the opening unrealised gain -- a quantity the table never prints -- so a misread in any of beginning market value, net earnings, transfers or change in unrealised breaks it. Worked example, PERPETUAL CARE BEQUEST: 199,002.91 + 1,503.09 + 4,201.40 + 9,600.00 + (1,098.80) = 213,208.60 ENDING CASH VALUE; 213,208.60 + 6,849.26 = 220,057.86 ENDING MARKET VALUE; and 206,862.08 + 4,201.40 + 9,600.00 + (1,098.80) + 493.18 = 220,057.86. TRANSFERS OF EARNINGS is printed in red and in parentheses where it is negative, and is recorded here as a negative number: only PERPETUAL CARE BEQUEST has one, (1,098.80), and it carries into the CEMETERY FUNDS subtotal unchanged.

rows.proof: `TOWN OF LUNENBURG DEBT REPAYMENT SCHEDULE AS OF JUNE 30, 2021` -- the PER-ISSUE DETAIL, PDF pages 43 and 45 of the FY2021 annual town report (printed folios 42 and 44). Fourteen debt issues against twenty-six fiscal years, FY2022 to FY2047: PDF p43 prints FY2022-FY2036 and PDF p45 prints FY2037-FY2047 plus a per-issue TOTAL column, which is read in the sibling group `fy2021-p45-debt-totals-by-issue.csv`. The GRAND TOTAL block these columns foot to is on PDF pages 44 and 46 and was proved independently by `fy2021-p44-debt-schedule.csv`. READ, NOT RECOGNISED: pdfplumber returns 0 words on both pages, and Vision's TSV is read a HALF-TURN OUT (pdf_tables.looks_flipped is True on each) and drops whole issues -- four of the fourteen have no figures at all in it. So every figure here was read off a 6x render, with ambiguous cells re-cropped at ~13x. FOUR KINDS OF ASSERTION. (1) The identity every issue-year states about itself, principal + interest + admin fee = the issue's total for that year: 189 of 198 close EXACTLY and the nine that do not are ALL three-summand Mass Water Pollution Abatement Trust rows and ALL out by exactly $1. (2) Each of the twenty-six years' four column sums against the GRAND TOTAL block on pages 44/46: every one of the 104 within $2. (3) Each issue's twenty-six-year sum against the TOTAL column printed on page 45: within $8. (4) The whole matrix against the printed GRAND TOTAL of the schedule, which is the `kind=total` row here. THE TOLERANCE IS $21 AND IT IS DECLARED FOR 198 TERMS OF ROUNDING, not for a doubtful digit. The schedule prints WHOLE DOLLARS over amounts carrying cents, so a printed total is the rounded sum and not the sum of the rounded parts; 198 terms at half a dollar each is a worst case near $99. WHAT SAYS ROUNDING RATHER THAN A MISREAD IS THE CONTRAST: PRINCIPAL -- bond principal, which has no cents -- ties EXACTLY at $41,885,307 across all 198 cells, while interest is out by $20 and the MWPAT admin fees by $4. A misread digit in these figures costs at least $1 and almost always $100 or more, and it could not hide: every bond cell sits in a two-summand identity that closes to the dollar AND in a year column that ties to an independently proved page within $2. ONE CELL WAS SETTLED BY THE PAGE 44 COLUMN TOTAL AND IS WORTH NAMING: DPW-ROADS GENERAL OBLIGATION, FY2024. The glyph after the first digit is a filled bowl that reads as 0 or 8 in both the interest cell and the total cell, and BOTH readings close the row ($250,000 + $30,300 = $280,300 and $250,000 + $38,300 = $288,300). The FY2024 interest column total on page 44 requires $38,300, and at ~13x the glyph has the pinched waist of an 8. Read as $38,300 / $288,300.
